paragraphs: R’ Nechemyah. (A Palestinian Amora, one of the teachers of aggadah.)
He spoke in R’ Abbahu’s name in Bereshit Rabbah [supplied פמ״נ־ד; the corresponding passage is at 43:3 in the consulted edition].

He and R’ Yehoshua speak in R’ Acha’s name at the beginning of the proems to Eichah Rabbah; with R’ Yudan in Bereshit Rabbah 59:7; with R’ Chananyah and R’ Pinchas in Midrash Tehillim 92:12; with R’ Azaryah and R’ Berechyah there in 24:5; and with R’ Nachman of Jaffa in R’ Yaakov of Caesarea’s name in Vayikra Rabbah 4:5.
He speaks in R’ Shmuel son of R’ Yitzchak’s name in במ״ר, chapter 50, section 2 [the specific work is unresolved].
And he is mentioned many times in the midrashim.

notes.text: פמ״נ־ד is an irregular supplied Bereshit Rabbah locator; the specific Midrash Rabbah intended by 50:2 is also unresolved. The old OCR conflicts remain preserved externally rather than silently changing those references.

No new primary scalar was returned. The Abbahu locator פמ״נ־ד and final במ״ר פ״נ־ב remain unresolved; the latter is retained visibly rather than confidently identifying a Midrash volume. The earlier finite Bereshit50:2 search miss does not establish global absence or prove that only Bereshit can have a chapter50. All supplied chapter/section readings and older machine פמ״ג״ר, פ״נט״ו, פ״ו״ה and דיפי conflicts remain preserved. Yerushalmi means Palestinian here, not exclusively a speaker in the Jerusalem Talmud. Every uninspected abbreviated personal title stays R-prime; Shmuel SON R-prime Yitzchak keeps both title and kinship.

Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 926) appears to cite Bereshit Rabbah 43:4 for Abbahu and Vayikra Rabbah 6:5 for the teaching with Nachman of Jaffa. In the consulted edition, the Abbahu transmission appears in Bereshit Rabbah 43:3. The Eichah Rabbah proem names Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Nechemyah in Rav Acha’s name, and Midrash Tehillim 24, in the consulted numbering, names Azaryah, Nechemyah and Berechyah together. The consulted Midrash Tehillim 92 attributes the count from a month old to Nechemyah and Pinchas, with no Chananyah in that clause. The exact final citation remains uncertain. Rashi on I Samuel 1:23 does cite Rabbi Nechemyah in Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak’s name, while the corresponding account in Midrash Shmuel 3 names Rabbi Yirmeyah instead.
